entities.name: PMID:10755546
observations: Primary study in mitogen-stimulated primary human T lymphocytes treated with 0.1–50 μM mycophenolic acid (MPA).
MPA reduced GTP to about 10% of unstimulated-cell levels and reduced ATP by up to 50%, with concentration-dependent effects.

Pyrimidine-related metabolism was altered: uridine pools expanded, CTP remained at resting levels, precursor incorporation changed, and [14C]-uridine uptake fell to unstimulated-cell levels, indicating impaired salvage rather than uniform global pyrimidine-synthesis blockade.

entities.name: Mycophenolic acid
observations: Inhibits IMP dehydrogenase and causes guanine nucleotide depletion; in the cited human T-lymphocyte study it also affected ATP and pyrimidine-related metabolism.

entities.name: MPA ATP depletion
observations: In mitogen-stimulated primary human T lymphocytes, 0.1–50 μM MPA caused concentration-dependent ATP reduction of up to 50% alongside severe GTP depletion.

entities.name: MPA pyrimidine effects
observations: In mitogen-stimulated primary human T lymphocytes, MPA altered pyrimidine-related metabolism: uridine pools expanded, CTP stayed at resting levels, precursor incorporation changed, and uridine salvage uptake decreased; this was not a uniform global pyrimidine-synthesis blockade.
